references.text: God promises Moses, 'I will be with you,' the same promise given to Gideon with the expression 'כִּי אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ' (for I will be with you).
The Lord promises Joshua to be with him, the same divine assurance of presence that Gideon receives.
God commands Joshua to be courageous because the Lord will be with him, parallel to the promise given to Gideon.
God's promise 'I am with you' as a basis for not fearing, the same theological theme found in Gideon's calling.
God promises Jeremiah to be with him to save him, corresponding to the promise to Gideon of divine support in battle.
The Lord promises to be with Jeremiah, the same assurance of divine presence that strengthens for service.
Jesus promises to be with the disciples all days, a New Testament fulfillment of God's promise of presence.
The Lord says to Paul, 'I am with you,' the same divine assurance that was given to Gideon.
Describes the great number of Midianites that Gideon was to defeat 'as one man' by God's help.
The fulfillment of the promise where God says he will save Israel by Gideon's hand and strike down the Midianites.
